findings.title: The control-protocol limb of CLAUDE-V1-B-2 is unrepaired - previewRequiredPairs is byte-identical to v1 - while the artifact records that the finding was folded and that nothing was left unfolded.
measured: previewRequiredPairs is unchanged from v1, verified by JSON equality: 'distribution core + TypeScript component + control major 1, each at N and N+1 as independently qualified bytes'.
basedOn.method lists /previewRequiredPairs on the 'Closed roster' of paths carrying targeted repairs. It is the only roster path that is unchanged.
honestyRepairsFromV1[1] records 'CLAUDE-V1-B2 / CODEX-V1-B1/B2: releaseIdentities + conformanceModel + passProperty records. Shared-version trains fail.'
appliesFindingsOf.notFoldedThisSuccessor is [] - an explicit assertion that no v1 finding was left unfolded.

The repair fields do not reach the control surface: releaseIdentities defines exactly two identities, coreReleaseIdentity and componentReleaseIdentity. conformanceModel.requiredRecords names core and component releases, skew tuples, rollback sequences, generation closures, and bundle records. The string 'control' does not occur anywhere in either field.

So previewRequiredPairs names THREE surfaces while the new independent-identity model grants release identity to TWO. The third named surface has no identity, no conformance record, and no pass property.

control-protocol-contract.v2, this artifact's own governingSources[2] with digest re-verified live: .compatibilityMatrixRow - 'supported readers = major 1 exactly (no cross-major window exists yet, and none can exist before a second major does)'; future-major refusal 'typed via the frozen refusal core (RF-1), never best-effort parse'; 'no in-channel downgrade path exists (RF-8)'. .handshake.ownVersionSurface - 'controlProtocolMajor = 1 ... NEVER a shared version with either provider protocol, the distribution core, or any component release.'
findings.whyItIsABlocker: The quantifier 'each at N and N+1' still has no bound stated. Under the distributing reading the preview requires a control-protocol N+1, i.e. controlProtocolMajor 2, which the consumed contract says does not exist, cannot yet have a cross-major window, and would be refused typed rather than interoperate - the preview is unexecutable as written. Under the non-distributing reading the control protocol is pinned at major 1 and is not a skew axis at all, in which case listing it inside an 'each at N and N+1' set is wrong and the pin is recorded nowhere. v2 makes this worse rather than better: by giving core and component explicit independent release identities and leaving the control surface out of that model entirely, it now names a surface in its preview scope that its own identity and conformance model does not cover. This single line remains the whole of the row's proposed preview scope on a row file 08 marks 'Hard blocker for independent-release blueprint'. The honesty defect compounds the technical one - a coordinator reading honestyRepairsFromV1 and an empty notFoldedThisSuccessor would conclude CLAUDE-V1-B-2 was disposed, when the line it targeted was not touched.
findings.whatWouldClearIt: Bind the quantifier explicitly: state which surfaces move N->N+1 in the preview and which are pinned. If the control protocol is pinned at controlProtocolMajor 1 because no second major exists, say so and cite control-protocol-contract.v2 .compatibilityMatrixRow; give the control surface either a release identity in releaseIdentities or an explicit exclusion with its reason; and correct honestyRepairsFromV1 and notFoldedThisSuccessor to record which limb of CLAUDE-V1-B-2 was folded and which was not.

findings.title: The COORDINATOR-DECISIONS pin asserts a v1-authoring measurement that v1 does not record and no artifact byte can corroborate.
measured: v2 records COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md at 12d192f7... with standing 'INHERITED-V1-AUTHORING-PIN' and measuredAtV1Authoring: true.

v1 records no COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md pin at all. Its governingSources has exactly three entries - file 04, file 02, control-protocol-contract.v2 - and the digest 12d192f7... appears zero times in v1. That absence is precisely what finding AL1-S-1 reported.

Dating the digest by replaying git history: 12d192f7... was COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md's content at commit 2327cf89 (D-100, 2026-08-14). It is a real historical state, consistent with v1's date, and it is the same digest a number of older sibling artifacts carry.

So the digest is genuine and the substance of the repair is delivered. What is not supportable is the provenance: 'INHERITED' implies carrying a recorded pin forward, and there is nothing in v1 to inherit; measuredAtV1Authoring: true asserts an act that left no trace in the artifact it is attributed to.
findings.whyItMatters: AL1-S-1 was an honesty finding about claims resting on unmeasured bytes. Closing it with a boolean asserting an unrecorded prior measurement answers an honesty finding with an unverifiable historical claim, in a file whose whole discipline is that a pin is a pin because it was written down. The practical risk is small - the cited entries D-002 and D-015 are old and stable, and reMeasurementAtV2 honestly discloses the drift to a28f7a23... at 9b06a2f - so this is a SHOULD-FIX, not a blocker.
findings.whatWouldClearIt: Record the entry for what it is: COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md as of commit 2327cf89 (D-100), named as a historical state rather than an inherited measurement, and drop measuredAtV1Authoring. Or drop the authoring-era entry entirely and rely on reMeasurementAtV2, which is accurate and commit-stamped.
